extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO personnel (attorneys, agents, examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Official Consolidated Patent Rules and select Manual of Patent Examining Procedure provisions governing filing, prosecution, practitioner conduct, and related procedures before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preissuance submissions by third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Preissuance submissions by third parties (see 1.290).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary amendments (see 1.115).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserved in confidence, applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications preserved in confidence (see 1.12, 1.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art citation in patented files / Prior art statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art citation in patented files; prior art statement: content of (see 1.98) and to comply with duty of disclosure requirement (see 1.56).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art submission by third party
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art submission by third party in patent application (1.290), in patent file (1.501), or in protest against pending unpublished application (1.291).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior invention affidavit / declaration to overcome rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior invention, affidavit or declaration of to overcome rejection (see 1.130, 1.131).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority, domestic benefit claim and cross-reference to related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority, right of, under treaty or law: domestic benefit claim; cross-reference to related application(s) (see 1.76 - 1.78).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules on filing fee in provisional, application data sheet requirements, and petitions for unintentionally delayed filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application formalities and conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications: claiming the benefit of; converting a nonprovisional to a provisional and converting a provisional to a nonprovisional (see 1.53(c)(2)-(3), 1.78).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover sheet required by §1.51(c)(1) may be a §1.76 application data sheet; filing date, filing fee, general requisites, later filing of fee and cover sheet, and identification of provisional application in papers are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee and application data sheet requirements for priority/foreign claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing fee must be paid in provisional application; indication whether international application was published in English must be on application data sheet (see 1.76(a), 1.78(a)(3), 1.78(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation of non-English provisional application may be required; petitions to accept unintentionally delayed claims; waivers if not timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fees and revival fees / fees for revival when abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing fees (see 1.17(q)); revival of processing fees and revival when abandoned (see 1.137(g), 1.53(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act — access, disclosure, exemptions, and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy Act provisions: denial of access to records, definitions, disclosure of records, exemptions, fees, grant of access, inquiries, medical records, penalties, requests for records, requests for correction or amendment, appeal of initial adverse determination, review of requests (see 102.21 - 102.34 and cross refs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document and time for claiming priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority document requirements and time for claiming (see 1.55, 102.21 - 102.34 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of application — early publication, nonpublication, republication
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of application: early publication (1.219), express abandonment to avoid publication (1.138(c)), fees (1.18(d), 1.213), nonpublication request, publication of redacted copy (1.217), republication (1.221), voluntary publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for published applications: access, certified copies, contents, definitions, preissuance submissions, and records open to public (see 1.11–1.15, 1.215, 1.221, 1.290).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance and reconsideration of Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for allowance (1.104) and reconsideration of Office action (1.112).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination — scope, conduct, processing of prior art, orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination procedures: order for reexamination by examiner (1.525), conduct of reexamination, scope, processing of prior art citations during reexamination (see 1.502, 1.902–1.997 for inter partes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes ex parte and inter partes reexamination provisions and filing/processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte proceedings — conduct, duty of disclosure, interviews, service of papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte proceedings: conduct (1.550), duty of disclosure in ex parte matters (1.555), interviews (1.560), service of papers (1.248), examiner’s action and determination to grant or refuse requests (1.515).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and fee administration (deposit accounts, refunds, surcharges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees: general fees (1.20(c)), fees charged to deposit accounts (1.25(b)), refund of fee (1.26), refund of money paid by mistake, surcharge for late-filed oath or basic filing fee (1.16(f), 1.53(f)), statutory disclaimer fee (1.20(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures and implicit certifications (S-signature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signature requirements: EFS character coded (1.4(d)(3)), handwritten (1.4(d)(1)), implicit certifications including S-signature (1.4(d)(2)); signatures required to a written assertion of small entity status, to amendments and other papers, to extension-of-term applications, to express abandonment, to oath and reissue oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a copy is acceptable (1.4) and rules surrounding signature acceptability are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity / micro entity status and statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Small business concern and small entity definitions (1.27(a)) and micro entity status (1.29); errors in status excused (1.28); fraud on the Office (1.27(h)); federal government use license exceptions; statement and statement in parent application; establishment and update of status (1.27, 1.28).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for declaring, establishing, and updating entity status, and consequences of errors or fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification content and arrangement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification requirements (1.71–1.75): abstract (1.72(b)), amendments to specification (1.121, 1.125), arrangement of specification (1.77, 1.154, 1.163), best mode (1.71(b)), claims (1.75), commencement on separate sheet (1.71(f)), contents (1.71–1.75), copyright notice (1.71(d)), cross-references, description of the invention (1.71), must point out new improvements specifically (1.71(c)), must refer by figures to drawings (1.74), must set forth the precise invention (1.71(b)), object of the invention (1.73), order of arrangement in framing (1.77).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must conclude with specific and distinct claim (1.75(a)), be separate from other parts of application (1.71(f)), and meet listed requirements; defective specifications may be corrected by reissue (1.171–1.178).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — must conclude with specific and distinct claim; species of invention claimed; restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must conclude with specific and distinct claim (1.75(a)); species of invention claimed addressed (1.141, 1.146); restriction practice and requirements for restriction (1.141–1.146, 1.176), withholding nonelected claims, constructive election, provisional election, petitions and reconsideration rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for subsequent presentation of claims for different inventions and withdrawal of claims to nonelected inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statements and continuing duty of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) (1.98, 1.555, 1.933): open to public (1.11(d)), reconsideration before final action, amendments, applicants/assignees responsibilities, continuing duty of applicant (1.178), declaration (1.175), drawings, examination of reissue, and filing during ex parte or inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for and requirements for IDS (1.171–1.178), filing fee rules, and public availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applications — no new matter, oath, processing and public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue: application for reissue (1.171), to contain no new matter (1.173(a)), oath (1.175), examination of reissue (1.176), original patent surrendered (1.178), multiple applications for reissue of a single patent (1.177), notice in Official Gazette, persons eligible to file request (1.913), processing of prior art citations during reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection procedures: applicant notified with reasons and references (1.104(a)(2)); after two rejections appeal may be taken from examiner to Board (41.31); final rejection (1.113); formal objections (1.104(a)(2)); references will be cited (1.104(d)); examiner may rely on admissions by applicant or patent owner or facts within examiner’s knowledge (1.104(c)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to Office action — timing, abandonment consequences, and RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply to Office action: time for reply (1.134, 1.135, 1.136); abandonment for failure to reply (1.135); reply brief (41.41); supplemental replies (1.111(a)(2)); representative capacity (1.34(a)); request for continued examination (RCE) (1.114) and fee (1.17(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules on substantially complete replies, supplemental replies, and suspension of action (1.103(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for reexamination (ex parte and inter partes) and scope of requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for ex parte reexamination (1.510) and inter partes reexamination (1.903, 1.913–1.927): scope, service of papers, processing during reexamination, replies to patent owner's statements, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of abandoned applications and unintentional abandonment fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Revival of abandoned application, terminated or limited reexamination prosecution, or lapsed patent (1.137); unintentional abandonment fee (1.17(m)); revival when abandoned (1.53(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings and sequence data format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences: amendments to sequence listing and computer readable copy (1.825, 1.835); disclosure requirements (1.821, 1.823, 1.831, 1.833); sequence data, symbols and format (1.822); submissions in ASCII plain text and optical disc options (1.52(e)(1)(ii), 1.821, 1.823, 1.831, 1.833).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers and service of process
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of papers (1.248) and service of process (15 CFR 15.1–15.3); service of notices in interference cases (41.106); identification in letters (1.5(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules — computing time, weekend/holiday adjustments, shortened periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Computing time and time periods (1.7): Saturday or Sunday/holiday adjustments when last day falls on a Saturday or Sunday (1.7); shortened period for reply (1.134); timeliness of filing correspondence (1.8, 1.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination of patents — content, conduct, and conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination of patents: content of request (1.610), filing of papers (1.601), format of papers (1.615), conduct (1.620), conclusion and procedure after conclusion (1.625), publication of certificate (1.67).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequences of rules for petitions, supervisory authority, suspension of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisory authority petitions to exercise (1.181(a)(3)); suspension of rules (1.183); petitions for supervisory authority regarding various procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions governing Part 11 practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for Part 11: attorney or lawyer; non-lawyer; belief; confirmed in writing; conviction/convicted; crime; data sheet; design patent practitioner; disqualified; federal agency; federal program; firm; fiscal year; OED Director; fraud/fraudulent; good moral character and reputation; grievance; informed consent; knowingly; law-related services; OED; partner; person; practitioner; proceeding before the Office; reasonable/reasonably; reasonably should know; registration; roster/register; screened; serious crime; significant evidence of rehabilitation; state; substantial; suspend/suspension (see §11.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many defined terms set the standards/thresholds for practitioner conduct, eligibility, disciplinary matters, and procedural application throughout Part 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition to practice before the USPTO and registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition to practice before the USPTO: register of attorneys and agents in patent matters; registration of attorneys and agents; requirements for registration; oath and registration fee; limited recognition in patent matters; restrictions on practice (see §§11.5–11.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative suspension, inactivation, resignation, reinstatement, and revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative suspension, inactivation, resignation, reinstatement, and revocation procedures (see §§11.11–11.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations and disciplinary proceedings — grounds and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations and disciplinary proceedings; jurisdiction, sanctions, investigations and procedures (see §§11.19–11.58 and related sections): warnings, disciplinary investigations, committee on discipline, reciprocal discipline, interim suspension, settlement, exclusion on consent, incapacity proceedings, diversion program, instituting a disciplinary proceeding, complaints, service and answers, contested case procedures, hearings, burden of proof, evidence, depositions, discovery, proposed findings, initial decisions, appeals to USPTO Director and further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct — competence and scope of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Client-practitioner relationship rules include: competence (11.101), scope of representation and allocation of authority between client and practitioner (11.102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets minimum professional standards for practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct — diligence, communication, fees, confidentiality, conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligence (11.103); communication (11.104); fees (11.105); confidentiality of information (11.106); conflicts of interest — current clients (11.107–11.108) and duties to former clients (11.109); imputation of conflicts (11.110); special rules for former or current federal government employees, judges, arbitrators, mediators, organization as client, and clients with diminished capacity (11.111–11.114).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes practitioner obligations in client relationships, fee arrangements, confidentiality, and conflict screening/imputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct — safekeeping property and termination/declination
rubrics_metrics.description: Safekeeping property (11.115); declining or terminating representation (11.116); sale of law practice (11.117); duties to prospective client (11.118).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counselor and evaluation duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselor duties include advisor functions (11.201), evaluation for use by third persons (11.203), and practitioner serving as third‑party neutral (11.204).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate rules — meritorious claims, candor, fairness, and trial conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate duties: meritorious claims and contentions (11.301); expediting proceedings (11.302); candor toward the tribunal (11.303); fairness to opposing party and counsel (11.304); impartiality and decorum of the tribunal (11.305); trial publicity (11.306); practitioner as witness (11.307); advocate in nonadjudicative proceedings (11.309).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for advocacy and ethical litigation/prosecution conduct before the Office and tribunals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transactions with persons other than clients — truthfulness and respect for rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Truthfulness in statements to others (11.401); communication with person represented by a practitioner (11.402); dealing with unrepresented person (11.403); respect for rights of third persons (11.404).

rubrics_metrics.name: Law firm responsibilities and non‑practitioner assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Law firms and associations rules: responsibilities of partners, managers, supervisory practitioners (11.501); responsibilities of subordinate practitioners (11.502); responsibilities regarding non‑practitioner assistance (11.503); professional independence (11.504); unauthorized practice of law (11.505); restrictions on right to practice (11.506); responsibilities regarding law‑related services (11.507).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications concerning a practitioner’s services and solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about legal services: communications concerning a practitioner’s services (11.701), specific rules on communications (11.702), solicitation of clients (11.703), communication of fields of practice and specialization (11.704), firm names and letterheads (11.705).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining the integrity of the profession — reporting and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining the integrity of the profession: registration, recognition, and disciplinary matters (11.801); judicial and legal officials (11.802); reporting professional misconduct (11.803); misconduct (11.804); related provisions for sanctions and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific defined standards of culpability and remediation (fraud, knowingly, serious crime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'Fraud or fraudulent' (material misrepresentation or omission, intent/recklessness and resulting justifiable reliance and injury); 'Knowingly/knows' (actual knowledge, may be inferred); 'Serious crime' definitions including felonies and crimes involving interference with administration of justice, false swearing, misrepresentation, fraud, etc.; 'Significant evidence of rehabilitation' standard for disability/rehabilitation outcomes (see §11.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set thresholds for discipline and fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner definition and categories of authorized practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner means: (1) an attorney or agent registered under §11.6; (2) an individual authorized under 5 U.S.C. 500(b) or §11.14 to practice in trademark matters or other non‑patent matters; (3) an individual authorized to practice in patent matters under §11.9(a) or (b); (4) an individual authorized under §11.16(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes who is authorized to appear/practice before the Office and is subject to Part 11 rules.
